pack.title: Dinner-table interrogations
pack.description: Holiday cross-examination with witnesses. Loving, brief, final.

scenarios.setting: Holiday dinner. Your aunt, passing the potatoes, loud enough for all.
scenarios.jab: So are you seeing anyone, or still too picky?

replies.line: I'm keeping that private. Let's enjoy dinner.
replies.why: It closes the private topic and redirects to the shared meal.
replies.delivery: Smile only if natural; finish the boundary and introduce another topic.

replies.line: Keeping that private. Pass the gravy?
replies.why: It gives a brief answer and redirects toward dinner.
replies.delivery: Smile only if natural; finish the boundary and introduce another topic.

replies.line: I'll share news when I'm ready; I'd love to hear about your trip instead.
replies.why: It preserves control of disclosure and offers a topic you welcome.
replies.delivery: Smile only if natural; finish the boundary and introduce another topic.

replies.line: My love life has a press office now. It declines to comment.
replies.why: The joke treats private disclosure as optional rather than required by the question.
replies.delivery: Smile only if natural; finish the boundary and introduce another topic.

trap.line: God, can we have ONE dinner without the inquisition?
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Keep your dating life private at a family meal.

followUp.jab: We just want you to be happy.
followUp.line: I appreciate that; I'll share news when I want to.
followUp.why: It accepts the caring intention without promising disclosure on demand.
followUp.delivery: Smile only if natural; finish the boundary and introduce another topic.

scenarios.setting: Sunday dinner. Your father, carving, without looking up.
scenarios.jab: When are you going to get a real job?

replies.line: It is my work. I'm happy to explain what it involves.
replies.why: It affirms the work without equating its worth with income.
replies.delivery: Keep “work” matter-of-fact and avoid proving your worth through income.

replies.why: The Dad at the end keeps it family while the sentence stays final.
replies.delivery: Say “Already got one, Dad” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense.

replies.line: It's real, I promise — want the two-minute version of what I do?
replies.why: Offering the explainer assumes curiosity instead of contempt, which invites him in.
replies.delivery: Keep “It's real, I promise” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly.

replies.line: It's so real it pays taxes.
replies.why: It affirms that your work is real through an ordinary reference to taxes.
replies.delivery: Keep “It's so real it pays taxes” light; let the joke stand without repeating it.

trap.line: You have NO idea what I do. None.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Ask for respect toward your work.

followUp.jab: It doesn't sound like a proper career.
followUp.line: I can explain what I do; I won't debate whether it counts as work.
followUp.why: It offers information without accepting a demeaning frame.
followUp.delivery: Keep “work” matter-of-fact and avoid proving your worth through income.

scenarios.setting: Dinner at your in-laws. Your mother-in-law, serving you extra.
scenarios.jab: You look thin. Are you eating properly at home?

replies.line: I'm comfortable with my choices. Let's leave body comments out of dinner.
replies.why: It makes a topic boundary without defending your body or eating.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “I'm comfortable with my choices” at a steady, conversational volume. ” with a firm ending on the boundary.

replies.line: I know you care; I'd rather we talk about something besides my body.
replies.why: It acknowledges concern while requesting a different topic.
replies.delivery: Keep “I know you care” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. ” with a firm ending on the boundary.

replies.line: My body isn't on tonight's discussion menu.
replies.why: The joke sets a dinner-table topic boundary without promising to eat more.
replies.delivery: Keep “My body isn't on tonight's discussion menu” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” with a firm ending on the boundary.

replies.line: No body comments over dinner, please.
replies.why: It states the immediate boundary without adding a personal judgment.
replies.delivery: Say “No body comments over dinner, please” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” with a firm ending on the boundary.

scenarios.goal: Redirect an unwanted comment about your body.

followUp.line: I hear that; I'd rather not discuss my body over dinner.
followUp.why: It acknowledges concern while setting a topic boundary.
followUp.delivery: Use warmth on “I hear that,” with a firm ending on the boundary.
